commits.message:
Classify Ogmios JSON-RPC error answers by code, not message text

The node's Ogmios session raised every JSON-RPC error answer as a plain Error, so the history owner treated a syncing node's era-mismatch (2001) or an expired acquired state (2003) as a terminal failure and exited. The ledger-snapshot reader and the startup protocol-status retry recognised outages by matching message prefixes, which broke as soon as an error was wrapped or reworded. Kupmios also marks every Ogmios error answer non-retryable because Ogmios returns HTTP 400 for all of them.

A shared midgard-core helper now decodes the answer code and maps it to transient or terminal per the Ogmios v7.0.0 sources. The node session, the ledger snapshot, provider retry and three DA committee clients use it, and the two string-prefix shims are deleted. Retries stay bounded at the owning operation; no client-level loop and no new terminal state is added.

Hold on an already-applied watcher rewind and bound rollback history to k

When the chain re-announced a rollback the watcher had already applied, the replacement equalled the durable frontier, the step rejected it as a malformed finality result, and the coordinator exited 70; every restart met the same announcement. An exactly matching, already-durable rewind is now a duplicate held with no write and no instruction, and every other refusal is unchanged.

The consistency history also grew with uptime until the 6,483-entry decode bound threw. Each observation and canonical-progress commit now retires history entries, and the observations and chain points backing only them, more than 2,160 blocks below the frontier, which no rewind within Cardano's k can reach. The bound stays as an invariant assertion. Owned frozen snapshots also reuse their observation index instead of re-parsing it on every operation.

Clear readiness reasons whose clearing path can stop being reached

Now that /readyz publishes every liveness reason, a reason whose only clear runs on a conditional path becomes a permanent false unready. The operator watchdog raised and cleared its manifest reasons only on ticks where a strike was due, so once the lagging operator recovered the reason stayed up forever; idle and wait ticks now re-verify on the gate's own retry cadence while a reason is raised, and a wait is cut to that retry. A control-plane hold-timeout streak was published until the same scope next held the permit cleanly, which a conditionally entered scope may never do; it is now published only while the scope holds or waits, or within three hold budgets of its latest timeout.

Pins the confirmation tick's decision against the undecided reason, each fiber's halt source at its call site, and a restart test that now kills the child only after the restarted child serves. Corrects stale 'refuses to continue' wording and records that the devnet journey's idle phase blocks on /readyz.

Keep a payload-level invalid foreign-tip verdict until a payload verifies

A foreign header whose retained payload failed verification was stored as invalid, but once that payload was gone the next replay re-derived the verdict as missing or Ready, so the window gate lifted the refusal and the commit could build past a block it had already seen fail. The replay now keeps a stored invalid verdict unless this pass holds a payload that verifies against the header; losing the payload or the passage of time never weakens it, and the row is never pruned while it holds the verdict.

Adds tests pinning the sticky verdict in both directions, malformed-row and failed-replay refusals, the inclusive window end, every event-kind root/count pair, and the commit worker's call into the gate with the earliest barrier as its ingestion watermark. Corrects the assess docstring: it reads stored verdicts only.

Add a devnet stack that deploys and runs the full lifecycle unattended

devnet-stack brings up an isolated Cardano chain, deploys the protocol,
and starts the operator node, the DA committee and the watcher under a
supervisor. It then drives deposits, L2 transfers and withdrawals
through to L1 payout using only the user CLIs, and runs chaos drills
that kill and restart each service. Every step is journaled so an
interrupted run resumes. Dist freshness is checked before reuse, and a
reserve float keeps the payout reserve funded during long runs. The
live-acceptance reference is updated to match.

Retry the watcher's transient L1 and retained-DA failures instead of exiting

The watcher exited on transient chain-sync, Kupo and retained-DA
transport failures. The supervisor restarted it into the same state, so
a merged header whose payload had been pruned put it into a permanent
crash loop. Transient failures are now classified in one place and
retried with a bound, permanent refusals are kept separate and reach
the operations alert book, and merged headers no longer need their
pruned payloads.

Keep the DA committee serving through provider, database and peer outages

Committee members exited, or stayed halted, on conditions that clear on
their own: an Ogmios or Kupo outage during the state-queue scan or the
rollback feed, a Postgres outage while the instance lock was held, a
peer that went away. Each of these now retries with a bound and reports
the outage through readiness instead of ending the process. The tests
cover the responder drain, a foreign spend of a challenge, and libp2p
payload handlers that leave state they do not own untouched.

Size commit selections against the full DA frame and step down on overflow

The commit planner budgeted DA bytes as the selected transaction bytes
plus 128 per transaction. It never saw the base-ledger UTxO aggregate,
the second copy of each transaction, or the CEK program material and
traces, and it checked the 16 MiB transaction clause first, so the DA
clause could essentially never fire. The pre-submit frame check sees the
whole payload and refused it. Selection is deterministic, so the planner
picked and refused the same over-frame selection on every tick, and
ordinary traffic on a large ledger halted production.

The planner now threads the base aggregate into its budget and selects
only what the pre-submit check admits. If a built block still overflows,
the worker steps down once, from a fresh fork, to a smaller selection
with an empty-block floor. The pre-submit refusal stays as the last
guard.

Re-land a signed intent whose sibling finalized and then lost its header

When a signed local block was replaced on L1 by a sibling that finalized
locally, and a rollback the node never saw as a confirmed removal then
took the sibling's header away, no admitted status matched the sibling.
abandonReopenedJournal failed, and the expired-intent decision returned
undecided on every evaluation. Block production stayed stopped until the
journal was repaired by hand.

The expired-intent release now re-derives its decision from the landed
chain. Before the TTL it waits. Once the TTL has passed it re-lands from
the base spend, following the ruling that whichever block lands wins,
and the correction rewind keeps a held retained chain and resumes it in
the same process once its authority returns.

Keep the operator node live through provider outages, restarts and rollbacks

The operator node had several ways to stop producing blocks until
someone repaired it by hand, and several holds that looked healthy from
the outside:

- /readyz never read the liveness reasons, so a node that had paused
  block production still answered ready. Readiness now reports each hold,
  and a stale incident is cleared once its condition goes away.
- A local-finalization job left Failed on a Finalized journal was refused
  at every startup, and each commit tick rewrote a Running job into that
  shape. Recovery now closes the job.
- The history owner exited on a lost signed-intent decision race and on
  rewind-proof gaps. It now waits and decides again.
- The worker cancelers that run under the L1 control-plane permit are
  bounded, and the permit holder is watched. Transient provider and
  database failures leave the node unready instead of exiting it.
- A foreign-tip verdict of invalid stays a refusal: the window gate never
  lifts it and the time-based prune never deletes it.

One identity race after the native CAS still exits the history owner. It
is fixed in a later commit.

Classify transient L1 provider failures in core, SDK and fault-proof readers

Ogmios slot evidence, event-history reads, singleton UTxO lookups, the
reference-script and payout reference fetches, and the fault-proof
Kupmios source raised plain errors for conditions that clear on their
own: a tip not yet reported, Kupo's datum index lagging a fresh mint, a
dropped socket. Every caller treated them as terminal, so a node,
watcher or prover stopped on a provider hiccup.

Each one now carries a typed, retryable classification. Conditions that
cannot clear by waiting, such as two authentic singletons or malformed
data, stay terminal. The module-size exceptions are re-pinned to the new
line counts.
Clean up README from the AI notes from the rewrite

Split oversized off-chain modules and cap ESLint at 500 lines

Reduce the concentration of large modules while preserving declaration
behavior, public exports, mutable ownership and entrypoint contracts.
Split 717 TypeScript, JavaScript, Go and Rust originals; ratchet retained
overages with exact per-file caps and documented reasons. No Aiken or
Plutarch sources are included.

The 2026-09-30 production inventory drops from 159 to 21 modules above
1,000 lines and from 45 to four above 2,000 lines. Extend source guards,
journey source pins and scenario reachability checks across extracted
implementations; preserve SDK ESM initialization and direct-source loaders.

Verification evidence, exact commands, counts, exit codes and limitations
are recorded in docs/module-size-refactor/verification.json and README.md.
Owned-file ESLint (3,159 files), workspace typecheck/build, all three
required transaction-preparation gates, tooling and native checks pass.
The original full preflight remains non-green (44 passed, eight failed).
Corrective runs resolve refactor regressions; migration/journey baseline
failures and one concurrent ledger-test failure are reported explicitly.
Live devnet/release acceptance and skipped opt-in cases were not checked.

Evaluate scripts over the maps the fault proof commits

The node built each script context as Lucid Data. Lucid's encoder sorts
every map and its decoder merges duplicate keys. The fault proof keeps
datum and redeemer maps in their CBOR entry order, duplicates included,
and orders the redeemer map by the witness list. The node sorted that
map. So a node could evaluate a script over a context the proof does not
commit. Two things went wrong:

- An order-sensitive script could get a verdict the proof contradicts.
- The trace builder failed closed with "context differs". That happened
  on any transaction whose datum, output datum or redeemer held an
  unsorted or duplicate-key map, or whose redeemers were not in sorted
  order. Such a transaction's fraud was then unprovable.

The context is now built as harmonic Data straight from the witness
bytes. It is encoded with the cardano-node encoder the CEK constants
already use. Harmonic's own dataToCbor is not used: it truncates byte
strings longer than 64 bytes. Redeemer data travels as its exact bytes
through the ledger transaction, its codec and the worker wire format.
The context's redeemer map follows the witness list.

Order the one-shot output Value like the script context

`script_value_data` passed an output's canonical asset map straight into the
TxOut Data it summarises. Canonical CBOR orders each policy's asset names
length-first, while the evaluated script context, the TypeScript context
commitment and the `ledger_output_value_v1` fold all order them by their
bytes. So for a policy holding names such as `aa` and `0102`, the one-shot
path behind `ledger_output_summaries_v1`, `ledger_output_descriptor_v1.build_v1`,
`tx_out_data_v1` and `tx_out_summary_v1` produced a different summary, and a
different descriptor, from the one every producer commits. No deployed
validator reaches this path; the blueprint is unchanged, 1163 validators with
identical hashes. Its callers are tests and fixtures, and a fixture with mixed
name widths would have been silently wrong. The names are now re-sorted; policy
ids need no re-sort, since the canonical decode admits only 28-byte policies in
ascending order.

`ledger_output_summaries_with_value_v1` let a caller substitute a Value summary
without naming what authenticated it, and only one test used that branch. It is
folded into `ledger_output_summaries_v1`. The staged transition-trace rules
already compose through `ledger_output_summaries_of_authenticated_parts_v1`,
whose comment now says what it reads and where its Value comes from.

The test that used the removed branch paired an empty-value output with an
unrelated 5,002-byte summary, so it pinned only how the parts compose. It now
folds a mixed-width Value through `ledger_output_value_v1`, composes it the
way the output-summaries step does, and requires the one-shot summaries. With
the old ordering it fails. A new negative test pins that the fold refuses to
finalize, or to skip to finalizing, while assets remain; letting a no-witness
step jump to the finalize stage passed every existing test in the module and
fails this one.

The sort adds execution cost only to tests that derive descriptors through the
one-shot path, so two execution ledgers are re-taken. In the transition-trace
descriptor ledger, deriving the descriptor of an output with no native assets
costs 666 mem more and the three-asset golden vector 27,850 mem more; each
deposit-arm derivation costs 9,546 mem more, and the L2 no-op arm's marginal
cost falls by 134 mem. No fit judgement or crossing bracket moves. The Q21 L2 no-op row rises by
532 mem and stays within the basis.
